root_idea.summary: The root centers on traces becoming faint, effaced, or difficult to perceive, and on repeatedly following a trace or path.
root_idea.development: From the effacement of physical traces and the repeated passage that wears or marks something, the root develops the sense of repeatedly following a text's traces through reading and study, leading to retention and learning.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Canonical Quran-attested Form I verb, normalized to the Classical Arabic perfect citation form.
A distinct Quran-attested verbal noun, normalized to دِرَاسَةٌ.

senses.definition: To read or study a text repeatedly, retaining or learning its contents.
senses.usage_conditions: Used with books, scripture, knowledge, or other written material; the repeated activity may include memorization and learning.

senses.definition: To study a text but leave its contents unacted upon.
senses.usage_conditions: Reported as an interpretation of وَدَرَسُوا مَا فِيهِ in 7:169; this consequence is an explicitly reported interpretation in that context, not a required feature of the ordinary verb.

senses.definition: To become effaced, obsolete, or dissipated, said of narratives, signs, or their traces.
senses.usage_conditions: Reported in Lane's discussion of alternative Quranic readings and interpretations; it should not be imposed on all canonical occurrences of the supplied QAC Form I group.

senses.definition: Study or sustained reading of a text for retention and learning.
senses.usage_conditions: A verbal noun denoting the activity expressed by دَرَسَ, especially repeated engagement with scripture or other written material.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become effaced, erased, or obliterated; said especially of a trace, house, or place whose remains disappear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The disappearance may result from wind, sand, or the passage of time.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To efface, erase, or obliterate something by repeated passage over it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with a wind, winds, people, traces, houses, or other things that are worn away through repeated action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a book or writing to become old or obsolete.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of physical wearing and effacement, distinct from actively reading or studying a book.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a garment or piece of cloth to become old and worn out; also, to render it so.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used both intransitively of the garment and transitively of the person or thing causing the wear.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To tread or thresh grain, especially wheat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sense is associated with repeatedly passing over grain; regional usage is reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To approach sexually or have sexual intercourse with another person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive figurative usage; the cited lexical construction does not establish a restriction on the object's class beyond the construction itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To break, train, or accustom a camel through repeated handling.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of training or disciplining a camel; the sense emphasizes repeated tending or returning to the animal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a woman to menstruate.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A euphemistic figurative usage explicitly applied to a woman or girl.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To teach someone to read, study, or learn; to instruct or lecture someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May take a learner and a book or other subject as objects.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To read or study with another, each helping or teaching the other; by extension, to confer or discuss a subject.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The reciprocal study sense may involve repeated reading of a book. It is also reported in a variant Quranic reading associated with reading or consulting with the People of Scripture.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put on old and worn-out garments.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An archaic figurative usage associated with wearing clothing that has become worn.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To study or read together, teaching one another until the material is retained in memory.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal construction involving joint, repeated study.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An obscure or scarcely perceptible road or way.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The road is conceived as one whose traces have become effaced.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A lesson or lecture.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural is دُرُوسٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A relic, trace, or mark of something that is being effaced or obliterated.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word denotes the remaining visible trace rather than the act of effacement itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An old and worn-out garment or piece of cloth; by extension, something worn out, such as a carpet, coat of mail, or sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may function as a substantive or as an adjective applied to worn objects.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A euphemistic name for the female pudendum.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical idiom associated in the lexical discussion with menstruation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Training, discipline, or habituation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal noun or abstract noun associated with repeated handling and training.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Alexandrian trefoil or bersim, a clover-like plant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separately attested lexical item despite the related form of the word.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Describing a house whose remains are becoming effaced or obliterated.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used adjectivally of a dwelling or its ruins.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A menstruating woman or girl.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival or substantive usage explicitly applied to a female person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A euphemistic name for the penis.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical idiom.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A conventional technical term or signification used in teaching or lecturing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized educational usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A book or piece of writing; also, a commentary used for teaching.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The commentary sense is reported as a secondary lexical explanation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place for reading or study, such as a college, academy, collegiate mosque, or synagogue.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can refer specifically to a Jewish house in which the revealed Book is read repeatedly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The road or track followed by camels or other livestock.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized expression for an animal route.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bed or resting place made level, smooth, and easy to lie upon.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative passive-participial usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person tried, strengthened, or made expert through use and experience.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to someone tested and seasoned by practice.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who reads or studies much and repeatedly; hence, a teacher, lecturer, or professor.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The educational occupation sense is associated with a teacher in a place of study.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who reads or studies the books of the Jews.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form conveys an intensive association with repeated study.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Describing a house whose remains have been effaced or obliterated.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participial description of ruins or a vanished dwelling.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Describing a road much beaten by travelers and thereby made easy to follow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sense develops from repeated passage over a route.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who studies or reads with another; also, one who has read books.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The first sense is relational, while the second emphasizes acquired familiarity with books.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A slight or limited case of mange affecting a camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare lexical specialization reported independently from the principal semantic branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thick-necked person or animal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported as an anomalous lexical branch outside the root's principal semantic development.

cautions: The interpretation of 7:169 as studying a text but abandoning its practical application is explicitly reported as an alternative contextual explanation, not as the obligatory meaning of every occurrence.

Lane records alternative Quranic readings involving effacement and reciprocal study; the artifact does not assign those readings modern verse locations beyond the independently supplied QAC locations.
